overview: The Interior & Exterior Design and Site, Safety & Security advisory teams met to review and categorize project recommendations regarding school materials, historical preservation, and site access. The teams discussed critical infrastructure needs, including durable building finishes, community use of facilities, and a secondary emergency egress path involving DCR land.

items.title: Project Schedule and Recommendation Framework
items.summary: The teams reviewed the project schedule as they enter the Preferred Schematic Report phase and established a traffic-light system to categorize prior feedback into given items, discussion points, and potential challenges.

items.title: Materials, Health, and Sustainability
items.summary: The committee discussed prioritizing durable, healthy materials like masonry in high-traffic areas and creating uniform flooring across the building to assist with mobility and visual processing.

items.title: Identity, Belonging, and School Pride
items.summary: Members advocated for a design that celebrates Medford history through flexible mural spaces and artifacts without being overly nostalgic, emphasizing that the building should be a living space that evolves with student creativity.

items.title: Flexibility, Roof Terraces, and Civic Use
items.summary: The team explored the use of roof terraces for learning and therapeutic gardens, while noting a critical need for the new school to provide the city with more public meeting and event spaces.

items.title: Wayfinding and Artifact Preservation
items.summary: Proposals were made for a dedicated history or archive room within the media center to preserve cataloged plaques, trophies, and banners from the old building.

items.title: Site Access and Emergency Egress
items.summary: The team emphasized the critical need for a secondary emergency access point, initiating ongoing negotiations with the DCR to potentially utilize existing fire roads or adjacent land for public safety vehicles.

items.title: Mobility and Transportation
items.summary: Discussion focused on improving MBTA bus access, providing sidewalks on both sides of access roads, and maintaining trailheads for the public while managing high school parking needs.

items.title: Fields and Outdoor Programming
items.summary: The committee reviewed the potential for bringing more athletic fields on-site and considered community suggestions for a mountain bike pump track and after-hours adult education in CTE shops.

items.title: Hydrology, Accessibility, and Logistics
items.summary: Engineers planned for spring geotechnical studies to manage stormwater on the rocky site, while designers committed to universal access principles beyond minimum code requirements.

items.title: Next Steps
items.summary: The advisory teams will reconvene in September to finalize recommendations and review the building committee's preferred design alternative.

subject: High School Design and Site Access Recommendations
